title: Work IQ: federated connectors for governed access to more data sources
summary: Hold: the licensing section treats federated connector licensing as unpublished even though Microsoft documents requirements for users querying federated sources. The variable cost rating also assumes that background Work IQ API billing applies while the body explicitly says that is unconfirmed. The roadmap details and listed administrative paths and commands are supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to enable Work IQ to use federated connectors for governed access to additional enterprise data sources.
claims.quote: Enable Work IQ to use federated connectors for governed access to additional enterprise data sources.

claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Graph", "Work IQ"]

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.

claims.claim: The roadmap targets November CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview target is October CY2026.

claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "federated" connectors; "Work IQ" "federated connectors" admin configuration. Opened federated overview, custom setup, management, Work IQ API and Foundry pages; no Work IQ-specific launch list, approval migration or surfacing details.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Federated Copilot connectors use MCP to fetch external data in real time.
claims.quote: Use Model Context Protocol (MCP) to fetch data in real time.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Federated connectors use the user's identity and the source system's permissions.
claims.quote: The source system enforces all permissions. Users can only access content they're authorized to view and make changes they're authorized to make in the original data source.

claims.claim: Federated connectors do not index external data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Don't index external data into Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Federated connectors do not copy source data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Federated connectors don't copy or store data in Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Existing federated connector management is in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Are managed and governed by admins in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Copilot uses live connector results in its responses.
claims.quote: Copilot selects relevant connector tools at runtime and uses the live results returned by the source to respond in the conversation.

claims.claim: Federated connectors use OAuth 2.0.
claims.quote: OAuth 2.0 and encrypted communication ensure secure access and authentication.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Where a connector supplies the tools, Copilot can create, update or delete data with user approval.
claims.quote: Can read data and, where a connector provides the tools, create, update, or delete data with the user's approval. Admins can audit activity in Microsoft Purview.
claims.fix: Add the qualification: 'The Researcher agent remains read-only.' Also acknowledge that https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/overview#types-of-copilot-connectors still describes federated connectors as read-only, whereas the cited federated overview documents write actions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: New write-capable connector tools default to Needs approval.
claims.quote: If a connector publisher adds a new write-capable tool or changes an existing one, the tool is set to Needs approval by default.

claims.claim: MCP server firewalls that restrict source addresses may need static egress IP allow-listing.
claims.quote: If your MCP server restricts incoming traffic by source IP address, configure its firewall to allow the static egress IP addresses used by Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is wholly unpublished for this capability, with existing connector licensing presented only as an unconfirmed possible rule.
claims.quote: Federated Copilot connectors are available only to tenants and users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license (or Microsoft 365 E7). They aren't supported with Copilot Studio licenses or Microsoft 365 Copilot pay-as-you-go.
claims.fix: Replace the blanket gap with: 'Existing federated Copilot connectors require a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence or Microsoft 365 E7 for users querying the source. Microsoft has not published whether this Work IQ capability changes those requirements.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/prerequisites. Set licensing.model to 'add-on' and make the notes state this existing requirement and the narrower Work IQ-specific gap; retain Work IQ API billing as separately labelled background.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ API use has published usage-based billing in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: The Foundry Work IQ preview page says a connector can require a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence for each calling user.
claims.quote: A connector can require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license for each calling user.

claims.quote: | Enable / Disable | Copilot > Connectors > Your connections | Turns an individual connector on or pauses it without removing configuration. |
